newsitem.title: USA: US FDIC chair Helfer submits letter of resignation.
newsitem.headline: US FDIC chair Helfer submits letter of resignation.

text.p: Ricki Helfer, chairman of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp since 1994, submitted a letter of resignation to President Bill Clinton on Friday, the agency said.
Helfer, the first woman to head a federal bank regulatory agency, said in the letter she planned to leave the FDIC by June 1 or earlier upon confirmation of a successor.
Helfer, a partner at the law firm Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher in Washington before joining the FDIC, said she had achieved her goals and was ready to move on.
"I would now like to spend time with my husband and family and consider new opportunities and challenges," she said in the letter to Clinton.
During Helfer's tenure, Congress passed legislation to restore the health of the depleted Savings Association Insurance Fund. The fund was fully capitalized October 1, 1996.

If Helfer leaves before a successor is approved, FDIC vice chairman Andrew Hove would take charge of the agency, a spokesman said. Hove acted in a similiar capacity after the death of former chairman William Taylor in 1992.
